Overview: Create an N \times N pattern as follows.
###########
#.........#
#.#######.#
#.#.....#.#
#.#.###.#.#
#.#.#.#.#.#
#.#.###.#.#
#.#.....#.#
#.#######.#
#.........#
###########
You are given a positive integer N.
Consider an N \times N grid. Let (i,j) denote the cell at the i-th row from the top and the j-th column from the left. Initially, no cell is colored. All cells are guaranteed to be colored after the operations; there will be no uncolored cells.
Then, for i = 1,2,\dots,N in order, perform the following operation:
- Let j = N + 1 - i.
- If i \leq j, fill the rectangular region whose top-left cell is (i,i) and bottom-right cell is (j,j) with black if i is odd, or white if i is even. If some cells are already colored, overwrite their colors.
- If i > j, do nothing.
Determine the final color of each cell.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N
Output
Print N lines. The i-th line should contain a length-N string S_i representing the colors of the i-th row of the grid after all operations.
Constraints
- 1 \leq N \leq 50
- All input values are integers.
